chunks: He it is Who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise — they are the foundation of the Book — and others allegorical. So as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow the allegorical part of it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation; and those who are firm in knowledge say: 'We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.' And none will be mindful except those of understanding.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The foundation or mother of the Book

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Muhkamat and Mutashabihat verses in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the epistemological foundation for understanding the Quran by distinguishing between clear legal verses (muhkamat) and allegorical ones (mutashabihat). It highlights that while the precise meaning of the allegorical verses is known exclusively to Allah and the 'Rasikhun fi al-'Ilm' (those firmly grounded in knowledge, often interpreted as the Imams), the deviant follow them for self-serving interpretation, whereas the faithful affirm all as divine truth.
